Forwarding Emma's request — SierraRx wants a concise MAP + acceptance-tests pack by Monday. Laura/Connor: can you draft the MAP template and the initial acceptance criteria? Key constraints: 4-week pilot, target close end of June, must include security evidence we can share.

Initial thoughts to include in the MAP (please iterate):
- Success criteria (must-haves):
  * Accuracy: >= 92% agreement with SierraRx clinical QA prompt set on our initial 200-sample eval (they'll supply prompts).
  * Latency: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 450ms for 256-token generation on Dedicated config (region: us-west).
  * Throughput: sustain 40 reqs/sec for 95th percentile of expected window with <10% error rate.
- Exit gates (examples): security review completed, performance baseline validated, no critical accuracy regressions.
- Acceptance tests (examples): model-forwarding A/B on 200 prompt samples, load test 30/40/50 rps, token-cost delta report.

I attached a MAP template to speed things up. Laura — please own the acceptance criteria doc. Connor — own the load/perf test plan and the runbook for re-running after any config change. Jordan — can you be on standby for rollout/ops gating?

Thanks,
Vivek
VP, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

Team — draft acceptance criteria and exit gates attached (sierra_map_v1.xlsx). Summary below. I kept things measurable and limited to must/pass (blockers) vs. nice-to-have:

Must-pass acceptance criteria (all required to move to contract):
1) Clinical quality: automated scoring >= 92% F1 on SierraRx supplied prompt set (n=200).
2) Determinism: top-1 response stability >= 95% for repeated runs with identical seeds/config.
3) Latency: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 450ms for typical 256-token responses under the Dedicated instance config we discussed.
4) Throughput: baseline sustained throughput >= 40 req/s for 10-minute windows while maintaining p95 latency SLO.
5) Security evidence: SOC2 Type II report + evidence of customer-scoped audit logs for the pilot environment.

Exit gates (examples):
- Blocker: any critical security issue or data handling finding.
- Blocker: accuracy below 88% on the 200-sample set.
- Soft fail: intermittent p95 spikes tied to cold caches — requires mitigation plan and rollback policy.

Acceptance tests (how we'll validate):
- Accuracy run: run the 200-sample prompt set, produce scorecard with examples of false positives/negatives.
- Stability run: 50 repeated runs for 20 prompt samples to measure determinism.
- Load run: staged load at 20/40/60 req/s for 15m each, observe latency and error rates.
- Security checklist: redwood_security_summary.pdf (attached) + SIERRA-procurement checklist.

Owner matrix (in the spreadsheet):
- Redwood: Laura (accuracy + scorecard), Connor (load/perf), Operations: Jordan (provisioning + rollback), Sales: Vivek (customer communication + signoff).

I'll mark items with due dates in the MAP. Emma — if this looks okay we can finalize and send a version for your procurement team to attach to the PO.

Laura Bennett
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: sierra_map_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet); Attachment: redwood_security_summary.pdf (pdf)]

Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: MAP & Acceptance Tests for Pilot — SierraRx

Quick technical notes to complement Laura's doc:

- Load test plan (short):
  1) Warm-up: 5 minutes at 10 req/s (to populate KV caches).
  2) Step: 15 minutes at 20 req/s; measure p50/p95.
  3) Step: 15 minutes at 40 req/s; measure p50/p95 and error rate.
  4) Spike: 10 minutes at 60 req/s to observe degradation behavior and fallback.
  5) Repeat baseline after reset to check for caching improvements.

- Metrics to capture: latency (p50/p95), tokens/sec, GPU util, error rate, cold-start % of requests, cost per 1k tokens during test.
- Quantization/Model variant checks: We will run the exact same sample set on the reference full-precision model and the quantized variant and include a delta report (accuracy + artifacts).
- Runbook: any p95 violations > 2x target during acceptance => immediate rollback to previous baseline model + root-cause within 48 hours.

Timeline suggestion:
- Monday (Jun 1): finalize MAP and acceptance criteria.
- Tue-Wed (Jun 2-3): provisioning and baseline smoke tests.
- Thu-Fri (Jun 4-5): accuracy + stability runs.
- Week of Jun 8: load tests and security checklist validation.
- Target signoff week of Jun 15 (allows procurement + legal to finalize).

If SierraRx insists on end-of-June close, we can compress but need quick procurement turnaround.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: load_test_plan_short.txt (text)]
